sumber: KSSM Form 2 English DSKP (CEFR-aligned). All passages and questions are written for the app.

topik.nama: 1. Grammar: Past Continuous and Past Simple

nota.t: The past simple describes finished actions (I visited Melaka last year). The past continuous describes an action in progress in the past (I was reading at 8 p.m.). Together they show an action interrupted by another: I was walking home when it started to rain.

v.c: Past continuous interrupted by past simple

t: was/were + verb-ing for an action in progress in the past.
Often interrupted by the past simple: I was reading when he called.
Irregular verbs: go → went, eat → ate, write → wrote.

nota.t: The present perfect (have/has + past participle) links the past to now: experiences (I have visited Sabah), recent actions (She has just finished) and situations continuing to now with for and since (We have lived here since 2015).

t: have/has + past participle: I have finished.
Finished time (yesterday, last year) → past simple.

nota.t: Conditionals: zero (facts), first (real future: If it rains, I will stay home). Relative clauses use who, which, that, whose and where. Prepositions of time (at, on, in) and place (in, on, under, between) must be chosen carefully.

r: If you heat ice, it melts.
If it rains, I will stay home.
The girl who won is my sister.

t: Zero: If you heat ice, it melts.
First: If it rains, we will stay home.
Second: If I had time, I would …

topik.nama: 4. Vocabulary: Phrasal Verbs and Word Meaning

nota.t: Phrasal verbs combine a verb and a particle: look after, give up, find out, put off. Work out word meaning from context clues, word parts and synonyms or antonyms nearby.

t: Phrasal verbs: give up, look after, find out, put off, call off.
Synonyms have similar meanings; antonyms have opposite meanings.

nota.t: Reading for detail means scanning a text for specific facts such as names, dates, numbers and places. Read the question first, underline key words, then find them in the text.
Inference means working out what the writer means but does not say directly, using clues such as characters' actions, words and feelings together with your own knowledge.
Speaking well means using clear pronunciation, suitable expressions for asking, giving opinions, agreeing and disagreeing politely, and taking turns in a discussion.

Good writing has a clear purpose and audience, an introduction, paragraphs with topic sentences and supporting details, linkers (firstly, however, finally) and a conclusion. Check spelling, punctuation and tenses.

t: Skim for the main idea, scan for details.
Use context to guess the meaning of new words.
Paragraph: topic sentence, supporting details, example.
Linking words: furthermore, however, in conclusion.
